commenti.body: It’s a very “John Cusack” character and I think the movie relies heavily on the personality he brings to the role to make the film entertaining, though I use the term entertaining loosely, kind of entertaining like a train wreck. At any rate, I like it, good movie.

I appreciate how much it channeled the anger of the time period in a way most movies weren't able/permitted to be. It's reach perhaps exceeded is grasp but I am still fond of it. To me it's less like Grosse Point Blank and more like Southland Tales.
Good point, it shares a lot of vibes that southland tales had

The problem with War Inc. is, well, almost everything, unfortunately.

The comedy bits aren't funny.  The plot doesn't make any sense.  The story and characters aren't compelling.  It fails on almost every level where Grosse Point Blank succeeds.

The one area where I will give War Inc. credit is the action.  The fight scenes are really well constructed.  One of the only jokes that made me laugh was the extremely meta bit with the bad guys making fun of a Steven Seagal movie for the overuse of stunt doubles, and the reason they can get away with a gag like that is you've been watching John Cusack actually do the fight choreography like a real action star.

I always thought it was a weirdly toothless movie. There’s something baffling about the mainstream anti-war comedies Hollywood put out during the Bush and Obama years — things like War Inc, Whisky Tango Foxtrot, War Dogs, Rock the Casbah, Men Who Stare at Goats — where they all end up being completely flaccid and unremarkable.

i agree, war inc. had that unique blend of dark comedy and social commentary that made it an interesting watch. the way it channeled the political climate of the time was quite compelling. definitely had that John Cusack charm.
